widget.instructions: Both lines pass through the origin. They make two angles, θ and 180° − θ: the acute one is asked for.

args.text: Two lines make two angles: θ and 180° − θ.

stem: Line L₁ has slope {{m1}} and line L₂ has slope {{m2}}.
Find tan θ, where θ is the acute angle between them.

hints.text: Two crossing lines make two angles that add to 180°. The acute one has a positive tangent.
Compute (m₂ − m₁) ÷ (1 + m₁m₂), then take its absolute value.

angle-formula-missing-modulus.text: A negative tangent belongs to the obtuse angle, 180° − θ. The acute angle needs the absolute value.

args.text: Your value is tan of the obtuse angle.

angle-formula-sign.text: Check the denominator: it is 1 + m₁m₂, not 1 − m₁m₂.

sign-error.text: The acute angle has a positive tangent: take the absolute value.

workedSolution.text: The ratio is negative, so it is tan of the obtuse angle. The acute angle has tan θ = {{t}} (θ ≈ {{deg|int}}°; the other angle is {{obtuse|int}}°).

angle-formula-missing-modulus.front: Why the modulus in tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)|?
angle-formula-missing-modulus.back: Without it you may get tan of the obtuse angle (negative). The acute angle's tangent is positive.

generic.front: Acute angle between lines of slopes m₁, m₂?
